clue.text: Bow in some pain due to getting stiff

indicators.note: in means the word for bow sits inside the word for some pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp bit of pain
a bow is an arch, as in a bridge's curve

explanation.surface: Someone stiffens up after bending over, suffering for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' wants to be bending forward; it is the curve of an arch.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating cloth with starch is the process of making it rigid, so it is a word for becoming firm.

clue.text: Set antidotes may be made up

indicators.note: made up suggests the letters of antidotes are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A pharmacist prepares fixed remedies to order.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed or posted in a position, as troops are positioned.

clue.text: Porter accepting very soft fruit

indicators.note: accepting means the beer word takes the musical letters inside it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, so ale
pp is pianissimo, very soft in music

explanation.surface: A railway porter takes delivery of some overripe produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a person carrying bags; it is a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A common orchard produce, round and crisp, grown on trees.

clue.text: An ecclesiastic tea with nothing fancy

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
plain means unadorned

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes his tea simple and unembellished.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman attached to a college, hospital or regiment is a churchman.

clue.text: Detain a number inside

parts.note: to intern is to detain, especially in wartime
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a number

explanation.surface: A police instruction: hold a certain number of people indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Situated within, the opposite of external.

clue.text: A music man's language

definitions.meaning: Sir Edward ... was an English composer of light opera
the tongue spoken in Berlin and Vienna

explanation.walkthrough: The music man is the English composer Edward German (1862-1936); the 's links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer's surname that is also the name of a European tongue.

clue.text: Article a girl's found faulty

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a miss is a young girl; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a young woman turns out to be wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of order or wrong is described as awry, the sense of this adverb.

clue.text: A plank craftily placed?

parts.note: a board is a plank of wood

explanation.surface: A wooden plank is cunningly positioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craftily' suggests cunning, but means on a craft, a ship; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship or other vessel, the craft of the clue.

clue.text: Concentrated, even in its refined form

indicators.note: refined form suggests the letters of even in its are reworked into a purer shape

explanation.surface: A substance stays concentrated even when purified.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly focused or thorough, applied with great intensity.

clue.text: Though stony, gets notice about credit

definitions.note: the adjective points to a noun for loose rocks on a slope

indicators.note: about means the notice word goes round the credit abbreviation

parts.note: to see is to notice
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A hard-hearted person still spots the mention of a loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Though' is a link; the definition is loose, pointing at mountain debris.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope of loose rock fragments below a cliff is all stones.

clue.text: Road surface that can cause a crawler to come to a complete stop

parts.note: an asp is a snake, a creature that crawls
to halt is to stop entirely

explanation.surface: A slippery road brings a slow-moving vehicle to a standstill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawler' suggests slow traffic; it is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac-like bitumen mix is laid as paving on highways.

clue.text: Chicken, perhaps, or duck in a roll

indicators.note: in places the zero for duck inside the word for a roll

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Poultry choice on a menu: chicken, or duck served in a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a cricket score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a male bird of the farmyard fowl kind, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: A single transaction would be best

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: A trader thinks one big sale would be the best outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect or optimal: the most suitable possible, an adjective like the superlative.

clue.text: Give new orders to the back row

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains or houses

explanation.surface: An officer barks fresh commands to the soldiers in the back line.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder things is to put them in a different sequence or arrangement.

clue.text: Making a cut in almost all of the sea-going vessels

indicators.note: Making says the letters that follow are being formed into something new, an anagram

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word all loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A shipyard is trimming costs across nearly the whole of its ocean fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' gives AL; with A, CUT, IN those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective concerns ships, sailors and navigation at sea.

clue.text: Set free a French woman trapped in the van

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: trapped in puts the woman word inside the word for van

parts.note: the lead is the front, the van
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman shut in a delivery vehicle is released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' looks like a vehicle; it is the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Let off a lead or restraint, freed.

clue.text: The record is between 500 and 100

indicators.note: between puts the word is inside the two Roman numerals

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a chart position somewhere in the hundreds.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray apostrophe before 'record'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a flat round plate, the short word for that.

clue.text: Company creating storm over scientific apparatus

indicators.note: creating suggests making something new from storm's letters

parts.note: on means over, as in a lid on a pot

explanation.surface: A firm causes uproar about its lab equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: A particle accelerator of the 1950s; storm's letters become SMOTR.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton accelerator built at Brookhaven, a piece of physics research machinery.

clue.text: Help upwardly mobile leader over advance payment, with sparkling results

indicators.note: in a down clue upwardly means the help word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid means help

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of mobile

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance

explanation.surface: A social climber pays upfront and gets glittering returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwardly mobile' reads as one social-climbing phrase, but it splits: 'upwardly' turns the help word in this down clue, and 'mobile leader' is a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorated with glittering paste or sequins, as a sparkly dress is.

clue.text: Completed the paper-work

parts.note: read as finishing forms, but meant as getting a newspaper ready for printing, or retiring a child at night

explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper jargon for finishing an edition and sending it to press.

clue.text: A period without money for stupid person

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the period's word goes around the money's letter

parts.note: a dot is a full stop, a period
L stands for pound, money

explanation.surface: Going through a spell with no cash makes one feel foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as lacking, but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce or blockhead, a slow-witted fool.

clue.text: "Myriads of hurrying thro' the lawn" (Tennyson)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: the missing word from a line of Tennyson's The Princess, small streams running across the grass

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a blank between 'of' and 'hurrying'; the answer fills it.
explanation.definitionFit: Little streams or brooks are the small flowing waters the poem describes.

clue.text: Reformed gambler

explanation.definitionFit: Improved, as a reformed character is; also a punter who wagers.

clue.text: Others in the Post Office can be really speedy

indicators.note: in places the word for others inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: Staff at the post office can work remarkably fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning very fast.

clue.text: Having caught the spirit, beat it!

parts.note: snared means trapped or caught
rum is a spirit, a strong liquor

explanation.surface: A drinker grabs the bottle and is told to get lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it!' reads as go away; it is the instrument you beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A side drum with wires across its lower skin is an instrument struck with sticks.

clue.text: Step indoors

parts.note: read as an invitation to come inside, but meant as one tread of a ... in a house

explanation.definitionFit: A single tread in a flight leading between floors of a building.

clue.text: Play time

parts.note: read as a break at school, but meant as the speed at which music is played

explanation.definitionFit: The rate or pace of a musical performance is its speed of beat.

clue.text: Some dismal tavern in a foreign country

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gloomy pub somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean island nation, abroad from Britain.

clue.text: A surprisingly chaste and loyal friend

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of a chaste come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A virtuous and faithful companion, to everyone's astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: In Virgil's Aeneid he is the faithful companion of Aeneas, a byword for loyal friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: The trusty comrade of Aeneas, whose name became proverbial for a faithful companion.

clue.text: One who handicaps the bay in more generous way

indicators.note: in places the bay's letter inside the word for more generous

parts.note: nobler means more magnanimous or generous
b is the racing-form abbreviation for a bay horse

explanation.surface: A racing official weights the bay horse in a kinder fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: In racecards a bay horse is listed as b. A nobbler drugs or injures a racehorse to stop it winning.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tampers with a racehorse to hamper its chances is the slang term here.

clue.text: Equestrian comment made in court

definitions.meaning: an addition to a jury's verdict, such as a recommendation

explanation.definitionFit: One who sits on a horse; also a clause appended to a verdict or a bill.

clue.text: In debt again, and tense in consequence

parts.note: over means again, as in do it over
drawn means strained or tense, as in a drawn face

explanation.surface: Someone back in the red and anxious as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: Having taken out more than the bank account holds leaves one owing money.
